newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says South Africa's racial wounds need time.
newsitem.headline: Pope says South Africa's racial wounds need time.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Monday that a great effort was still needed in post-apartheid South Africa to heal racial divisions.
"Certainly, the wounds of the past will take a long time to heal and much effort will be needed to bring about a real and transforming reconciliation," he told South African bishops.
Leaders of South Africa's Roman Catholic Church were at the Vatican for an audience with the Pope which prelates from all over the world attend every five years.
The Pontiff, who celebrated his 77th birthday on Sunday, said South Africa had to continue to foster the nation-building atmosphere he had witnessed during a 1995 visit.
"During my brief visit to South Africa in September 1995 I had firsthand experience of the new spirit animating the country's people and their leaders," the Pope said.
"While enormous problems remain to be solved, there is renewed enthusiam for building a nation of freedom and justice for all," he added.
President Nelson Mandela and his predecessor F.W. de Klerk were jointly awarded the Nobel peace prize in 1993 for ending oppressive white-minority rule in South Africa.
